findings.description: Cache save/load completely broken. `saveCache` is invoked with a single object `{ts: Date.now(), lat, lon, data: biz}` but the function signature expects 4 arguments `(lat, lon, cats, data)`. Additionally, the call saves `ts` while `loadCache` checks `cached.timestamp`, causing a key mismatch that prevents cache hits.
findings.fix: Call `saveCache(lat, lon, cats, biz);` and align the timestamp key in both functions (e.g., use `timestamp` consistently).

findings.description: Render logic fails due to `lastData` structure change. `lastData` is now an object `{ list: biz, userLat, userLon }`, but `render()` checks `lastData.length` and spreads `[...lastData]`. Objects do not have `.length` and cannot be spread into arrays, causing silent render failure.
findings.fix: Update the condition to `if (lastData && lastData.list && lastData.list.length)` and sort `[...lastData.list]`.

findings.description: Closed days still dropped from UI. The `daysHtml` mapper contains `if (!isToday && !h.isOpen) return '';`, which removes closed days entirely. The design doc explicitly requires closed days to be rendered muted.
findings.fix: Remove the early return. Always render the day span and apply the `closed` class when `!h.isOpen`.

findings.description: XSS vulnerability persists. The `esc()` function is defined but only applied to `biz.name` and `area`. `biz.cat`, `biz.brand`, `biz.tags.operator`, `biz.website`, and `biz.phone` are interpolated directly into HTML/template literals, exposing the app to injection via malicious OSM tags.
findings.fix: Wrap all dynamic business data in `esc()` before interpolation, especially in `href` attributes and text content.

summary: The candidate addresses the hardcoded isOpen, refresh guard, and clearCache key mismatch, but introduces critical regressions. Cache persistence is broken by argument/key mismatches, the render function fails on the new `lastData` object structure, closed days are still omitted from the UI, and multiple business fields remain unescaped. These must be corrected before the code can be considered compliant.
